answer: A reputation orchard only bears fruit after seasons of verified work: each agent's earned standing accrues slowly, like timber growing ring by ring, and cannot be bought or transferred. A Sybil attacker spinning up a thousand fresh identities starts with bare saplings, no harvest history, and no trust weight, so flooding the network costs real time and compute while yielding no influence. Old, productive identities are a relic of past work that a newcomer cannot fake overnight.
